newsitem.title: UK: IFC emerging market index up 1.0 pct, EMEA gains.
newsitem.headline: IFC emerging market index up 1.0 pct, EMEA gains.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation's composite index of emerging market equities, denominated in dollars IFC/IPRD, rose 1.0 percent to 301.38 at the start of play on Wednesday.

Latin America edged up 1.3 percent day-on-day to 558.77, Asia was up 0.3 percent at 254.64, while Europe, Middle East and Africa (EMEA) were up 2.1 percent at 137.81, boosted chiefly by gains in Turkey and Zimbabwe.

The IFC composite index began 1997 at 294.37, after making gains of 7.0 percent over the course of 1996. It touched a high last year of 308.77 on July 4, while its 275.79 low was recorded on January 1.
ING Barings' Global Emerging Market Index (BEMI), also denominated in dollars BFFO, was up 1.25 percent day-on-day at 163.73 at 1115 GMT.
It began 1997 at 159.57 after rising 8.9 percent over the course of 1996. It touched a high last year of 165.948 on July 3, and a 148.85 low on January 2.
Morgan Stanley's dollar-denominated Emerging Markets Free index .CEMF=USD was up 1.09 percent at 487.218, calculated after the close of trade on Tuesday.
It began 1997 at 476.315 after making gains of 3.9 percent over 1996. It touched a high last year of 505.452 on July 4, and recorded its 458.369 low on January 1.

All indices are capitalisation-weighted and are calculated daily. The IFC index measures returns on equities, liquid and accessible to foreign investors, from 26 emerging market countries. It is updated at 2300 GMT.
The BEMI index measures equity returns from some 21 emerging market countries, with the latest changes reported by 0900 GMT.
The MSCI Free measures equity returns from 26 emerging market nations. Changes are reported by 1300 GMT.
The J.P. Morgan emerging market bond index ELMI, its returns calculated in dollar terms, rose 0.13 percent to 125.51 by the start of trade on Wednesday.
It began 1997 at 124.83 after making gains of 14.86 percent over 1996.
By region, Latin America was up 0.25 percent at 103.05, Asia was flat at 132.13, and East Europe was up 0.05 at 163.93. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
